strengths: Clear theoretical contribution with Theorem 1 providing formal KL divergence guarantees on approximating the optimal tilted policy, grounding the approach mathematically
Elegant core insight: tilting rewards by log-likelihood ratio log(π_B/π_S) is intuitive and theoretically motivated, elegantly accounting for model differences
Consistent empirical improvements over RSD and S-BoN(π_S) across all three mathematical reasoning benchmarks (51.1-51.3% vs 48.5-48.8% mean accuracy)
Practical efficiency: achieves 0.88-2.05s per step with GSI vs 1.14-2.76s for S-BoN(π_B), enabling real speedups on reasoning tasks
Well-organized presentation with clear algorithm specification, transparent experimental setup, and available code
weaknesses: Significant theory-practice gap: Theorem 1 covers π^{r,n}_{β,S} but Algorithm 1 adds unjustified rejection sampling step (lines 7-14) not covered by theory; Theorem 2 is much weaker, only showing convergence as n→∞
Theoretical bounds appear impractical: required n scales exponentially in β∥r∥_∞ (factor e^40 with given hyperparameters), suggesting bounds are loose and may lack practical utility
Insufficient experimental rigor: only 2 random seeds without error bars or significance tests, making it unclear if improvements are meaningful; differences often 1-3% within noise margins

Overstated claims about outperforming S-BoN(big): paper claims GSI 'surpasses' big model in some cases, but OlympiadBench shows S-BoN(big) achieving 42.5% vs GSI 41.2% at n=64, and Minerva Math shows 29.6% vs 36.4%
Strong coverage assumption (Eq. 3) treated superficially: critical for all guarantees but requires π_B support ⊆ π_S support; deserves deeper discussion of practical validity and failure modes
No hyperparameter sensitivity analysis: β and threshold u identified as empirically selected with no ablation studies, sensitivity analysis, or principled selection guidance provided
Limited experimental scope: only mathematical reasoning with Qwen models; generality to other domains (alignment, safety) and model sizes/architectures unvalidated
Incomplete scaling analysis: Figure 2 stops at n=256 despite acknowledged need to investigate beyond, limiting understanding of convergence behavior
Missing comparisons: no evaluation against other recent test-time scaling methods beyond RSD, limiting positioning in the literature
